_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 15 (the Covenant Between the Pieces). Saadia-specific moves: v.1 בוחי = 'by revelation' (substitutes for 'במחזה' = 'in a vision'); v.6 כתבהא לה חסנה = 'counted it to him as a good [deed]' (substitutes 'good deed' for the abstract 'righteousness'); v.11 striking interpretive move on וירד העיט — Saadia takes the singular bird (= the undivided dove/turtle from v.10) as the subject, and reads וישב as causative 'Abram moved them' (the carcasses) — rationalizes the eerie scene as ritual placement, not threat from vultures; v.13 'תמאם' = 'the full' (intensifies the four hundred years); v.20 רפאים=אלשגעא 'the mighty ones' (consistent with B14:5).

translations.1: After these things, the word of God came to Abram by revelation, saying: 'Fear not, O Abram; I am your shield; your reward is exceedingly great.'
translations.2: He said: 'O God, my Lord, what will You give me? — for I am going forth barren; and the steward of my household is Eliezer of Damascus.'
translations.3: And Abram said: 'Since You have not granted me offspring, the son who is in my household shall inherit me.'
translations.4: And behold, the word of God came to him, saying: 'This one shall not inherit you; rather, he who shall come forth from your loins — he shall inherit you.'
translations.5: Then He brought him outside, and said to him: 'Turn your gaze toward the sky, and try to count the stars — can you count them?' Then He said to him: 'So shall your offspring be.'
translations.6: And he believed in God; and He counted it to him as a good deed.
translations.7: And He said to him: 'I am God, who brought you out from the furnace of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to possess it.'
translations.8: He said: 'O God, my Lord — by what shall I know that I shall possess it?'
translations.9: He said to him: 'Bring me a heifer three years old, and a she-goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtle-dove and a young pigeon.'
translations.10: And he brought for Him all of these, and divided them in their midst, and placed each piece opposite its fellow; but the bird he did not divide.
translations.11: Then he placed the bird upon the carcasses; and Abram moved them, and they stirred.
translations.12: And when it was at the time of sunset, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, an awe — a great darkness — had fallen upon him.
translations.13: And He said to Abram: 'Know assuredly that your offspring shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs; and they shall be enslaved by them, and they shall afflict them — for the full four hundred years.
translations.14: And the people whom they shall enslave — I, too, shall judge them; and after that they shall come forth with great possessions.
translations.15: And you shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.
translations.16: And the fourth generation shall return hither — for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.'
translations.17: And when the sun had gone down, and there was darkness, behold — like a smoking furnace and a flaming brand which passed between those pieces.
translations.18: On that day God made a covenant with Abram, saying: 'To your offspring I give this land — from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates;
translations.19: the Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
translations.20: and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the mighty ones (Rephaim),
translations.21: and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.'
